title: Its so much fun trying out different visual styles in a familiar environment, I'm trying to come up with an artstyle for my own project.
author: Terry__Poppins
selftext:
I'm working on a little solo dev project for a pretty simple game (can't say much more it would be an easy idea to copy) and one of the most important things for me is going to be to nail the artstyle. 

I'm looking at other games I admire for their vibe and strong art direction and trying them out by testing out what dust 2 would look like in that style. Made with Nano Banana via DaVinci AI, haven't really experimented with all the different models. If anyone knows which models work best for game concept art like this (ingame render style) let me know. If anyone has any pointers on how I could come up with something interesting for my project let me know, I wanna do something really interesting with the visuals.

comments.author: Covoh
comments.body:
I agree! However, implementing it into a game engine using AI can be frustrating. I know this because it's exactly what I'm doing at the moment for my game! Thankfully after over a week of back and forth I got to a point where it's just tweaking and Blender baking. 

For rendering I use Claude Code and Blender, but I highly recommend generating multiple examples of your chosen style including textures, close ups, and different angles. Don't expect a one-shot though.

replies.author: Terry__Poppins
replies.body: I haven't gotten to the part of implementation yet, still trying to figure out what kind of style fits my game best. But thanks for the advice, I definitely wanna do something like that when the time comes.

replies.author: Covoh
replies.body:
Another thing, rendering your concept art (once you get to that stage) will vary in difficulty depending on if your game will be 3D or 2D and for what platform you're going for, whether it'll be mobile or PC. So keep that in mind because doing full 3D renders and adding them to the game with high LOD will take up a lot of space, especially if every asset is high LOD, can even impact frames and performance. So you'll need to get creative and make sacrifices. 

Best of luck on your journey!

comments.author: Space-Gadget-Wizard
comments.body: Very cool, I like the one in the Okami style (on the top left) the most. It's so subtle but you can almost feel the brushwork from the original carry over.

replies.author: Terry__Poppins
replies.body: That one fits the best with the dust 2 aesthetic for sure, I like the bottom right too, that one is like Return of the Obra Dinn 1-bit dithering.
